meta.title: Before the thread fix: 8 files per trigger, run 1 only
meta.explanation: In these runs only PyTorch was held to one thread per worker (`torch.set_num_threads(1)` in the model loader); the OpenMP, MKL and OpenBLAS thread pools that numpy and torch set up were still sized to the 12 hardware threads, so `local[n]` started n Python workers that could each spawn several math threads. As n grew these threads competed for the same 12 hardware threads and caches (oversubscription), while every worker also held its own copy of PyTorch and the models, so throughput *fell* from 6,280 records/s at 1 core to 3,190 at 8 (and the laptop was already short of memory, which made it worse). The main result below sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS` and `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` to 1 before the SparkSession starts, so every local-mode worker inherits one math thread.
meta.note: first of two planned runs; run 2 was slowed by memory pressure and then stopped, so only run 1 is kept
